propositions: A single pending entry in the queue disables the marker's O(1) fast path for the entire store, causing every subsequent write to perform a full O(store) directory walk until the pending set empties

The marker is currently written only when a full scan finds nothing pending, and not written when pending entries exist, creating an all-or-nothing binary trigger rather than a proportional cost model

The generalized marker design records a live set of ticket IDs with enqueued entries, allowing scoped O(backlog) reductions instead of full O(store) walks while preserving TTL-bounded staleness bounds from the last full scan
Scoped marker probes must not rewrite the marker to preserve the TTL contract that measures time from the last full walk, not from each probe
New queue appends still clear the marker to maintain honesty: the marker only asserts absence of pending work and never manufactures a false pending verdict
